engineering_constraints.description: Pyrolysis: 500°C under N₂ (80 mL/min) for 120 min

narrative.text: Plant-derived biochar converts agricultural waste into carbonaceous adsorbent via pyrolysis. Surface modification with silicate, phosphoric acid, or alkali enhances adsorption capacity. Low-cost and sustainable approach for heavy metal removal.

design_translation.idea: Pyrolyze agricultural waste (rice straw, oiltea shell, walnut shell) at 500°C to create biochar adsorbent, with optional surface modification for enhanced performance
design_translation.design_principle: Lignocellulosic architecture provides multiple functional groups (hydroxyl, carboxyl, phenolic) for metal ion and dye adsorption
design_translation.implementation_example: Silicate-modified oiltea shell biochar: 211 mg/g for Cd; Walnut shell biochar for tetracycline removal
design_translation.constraints: Structural rigidity may limit adsorption capacity; pretreatment may be needed
design_translation.failure_modes: Low adsorption capacity without chemical modification
material_realization_examples: Silicate-modified oiltea shell biochar: 211 mg/g for Cd
Walnut shell biochar for tetracycline removal
design_translation.target_interaction: metal ion and dye adsorption via functional group coordination
